title: Stars, Cows and Dogs Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 19
description:
Laddoo Lab now sells five things, but Zoya has money for only one big push. Which product should get it, and should anything be dropped? In this animated lesson we use the Laddoo Lab range from a Bengaluru home kitchen to understand product portfolio management.

You will see what a product portfolio (Kotler's product mix) is, with its width, length and depth, and then a live run of the growth-share matrix that Bruce Henderson of the Boston Consulting Group made famous in 1970. We place each Laddoo Lab product as a star, a cash cow, a question mark or a dog, and watch the cash flow from the cow to the star and the chosen question mark. We cover the four moves (build, hold, harvest, divest) and the matrix at work today in a phone maker, a bank, a food delivery app and an airline. The human side: the matrix shows the whole range at once, but it uses only two measures, a dog can still bring in new customers, and a 1992 study by Slater and Zwirlein found weaker shareholder returns for firms that invested by such a portfolio model.

This is Episode 19 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
